assumptions: The IPC caller-locking prerequisite keeps the selected object and refcount storage valid throughout the modeled retry operation.
The selected operation is scheduled through every modeled loop step and once after the finite interference schedule quiesces; this is a bounded scheduling premise, not general fairness.
atomic_try_cmpxchg_relaxed has the selected Linux strong, non-spurious compare/exchange semantics and updates old to the current counter on mismatch.

At most three interference observations occur before quiescence; initial and interfering values remain in the explicit zero-through-three domain, and a successful terminal increment may produce four, so saturation and arithmetic overflow are unreachable.

Each selected x86 CMPXCHG or s390 CS instruction completes according to its architectural compare/exchange semantics, including loading the observed word into the s390 comparison operand on mismatch; hardware failure and global machine liveness are not established by the C-source gate.

progress.claim: For the selected native x86-64, s390x and UML x86-64 ipc_rcu_getref() implementations, if refcount_inc_not_zero() is scheduled through at most three interfering counter observations and once after interference quiesces, its strong-CAS source loop returns after at most four compare/exchange attempts; an initially or newly observed zero returns without resurrection.
exclusions: Unbounded interference and per-thread starvation are excluded; no wait-free or general lock-free guarantee is claimed.
Spurious compare/exchange failure is excluded by the selected strong API semantics; weak CAS is not modeled.
LL/SC implementation progress and architectures beyond the selected native/UML x86-64 and s390x objects are not accepted by this progress property.
Saturation, overflow, underflow, warning paths, RCU callback progress and allocator lifetime are outside the finite-state model.
No general scheduler fairness, CPU forward-progress, whole-IPC, whole-RCU or whole-kernel liveness property is claimed.

property.claim: For a locking-stabilized System V IPC object whose refcount starts at one, one selected ipc_rcu_putref() and one concurrent selected ipc_rcu_getref() cannot both schedule last-reference RCU destruction and return a successful reference acquisition.
exclusions: The caller-locking and pointer-stability prerequisite is assumed, not proved; an attempt through already reclaimed storage is outside the property.
The initial refcount is exactly one, there is one selected get and one selected put, and no third refcount update is modeled.
RCU grace periods, callback execution, allocator reuse, ABA and SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU behavior are not modeled; call_rcu is represented only by the successful final-put decision.
Saturation, overflow, underflow, warning paths and values outside zero, one and two are excluded.
The acquire-after-control-dependency orders later destruction work but cannot change the selected same-refcount mutual-success outcome, so cross-object ordering is not claimed.
The unsafe resurrection case is a detecting control and is permanently ineligible as verification evidence.

No architecture implementation other than the eleven configured SMP x86-64, arm64, riscv64, s390x, ARM32, PowerPC32, SuperH, Alpha, LoongArch64, MIPS32 little-endian and UML x86-64 profiles is accepted by this source-linked pilot; every other architecture remains outside the claim.

The lifetime mutual-exclusion model itself claims no progress, fairness or retry bound; only the separate bounded-quiescent progress property below is eligible, and it does not establish general lock-freedom, wait-freedom, whole-IPC correctness, whole-RCU correctness or whole-kernel race freedom.
property.implementation_argument: The pinned LKMM treats the selected updates as indivisible RMWs. Configured x86-64, arm64, riscv64, s390x, ARM32, PowerPC32, SuperH, Alpha, LoongArch64 and UML x86-64 SMP objects preserve that implementation shape through their native atomic compare/exchange and fetch-sub paths before the final-put call_rcu branch; emitted alternatives, the explicit LoongArch Clang/LLVM route and UML's explicit x86 header route are checked rather than collapsed.
property.lifetime_argument: The final decrement schedules RCU destruction only when refcount_dec_and_test() observes the 1-to-0 transition; refcount_inc_not_zero() cannot acquire a reference from zero.
property.model_argument: With initial value one and exactly one competing get, the refcount get loop can succeed only in its first compare/exchange from 1 to 2; a failed compare means the sole decrement already installed zero, so the single relaxed cmpxchg is behaviorally exact for this outcome.
property.stability_argument: The pinned IPC contract requires caller locking; the property assumes that prerequisite keeps ptr and its refcount storage valid for both selected operations.
